subject: Fanout-induced latency spike — resilience plan & customer comms
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 30 May 2029 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: [Alert] Fanout spike on gen-api (p99 7.4s) - initial diagnostics attached

Team —

We started seeing a correlated p95/p99 rise on gen-api at ~09:05 PT. Quick summary from the first pass: 
- p50 ~ 180ms (normal)
- p95 jumped to ~1.1s for a 10-minute window
- p99 spiked to 7.4s (tail visible primarily on fanout-heavy routes: /v1/generate with multi-tool calls)
- Throughput steady, but we saw increased retries from downstream logging services that coincided with higher fanout attempts

What the runtime is reporting: multiple requests are triggering wide fanout (avg 6 replicas) because customer requests include multi-tool calls + long context (~2.2k tokens). We also observed heavier KV cache miss rate for those routes — likely due to recent cache invalidation rollouts in the last patch.

Immediate work in progress (SRE):
- Rolling restart of a small pool to force coldstart degeneration checks (in case of kernel scheduling backlog)
- Short-term circuit breaker: we have a feature flag to cap per-request fanout to 3 on the gen-api gateway; toggle ready but need approval to enable for affected tenants
- Reverting the recent cache invalidation change is a candidate but requires product signoff (affects correctness guarantees for some customers)

Attachments: diagnostic_snapshot-20290530.log (filtered stack traces + sampling traces)

Asks:
1) Product: recommend a conservative public-facing mitigation we can enable immediately (fanout cap + note about potential throughput reduction). We need guidance on whether to revert cache invalidation or opt for guard rails first.
2) Eng/Karthik: if we enable fanout cap, estimate of expected p99 impact and any downstream risk (loss of quality for multi-tool flows).
3) CS/Grace: prepare a short customer note we can send to affected customers if we flip the flag (see template in /cust_brief_draft-20290530.md).

Irene — looping you for prioritization and exec visibility.

—Ben

Ben Carter
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 30 May 2029 09:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [Alert] Fanout spike on gen-api (p99 7.4s) - immediate prioritization

Thanks Ben — good catch. Quick responses and asks from product leadership: 

- Marissa: please weigh in on the cache invalidation rollback. If the invalidation was rolling out as part of a correctness fix, we need a scoped rollback that preserves correctness for customers who rely on the change. If it's safe to rollback for affected tenants only, proceed; otherwise prefer conservative guardrails.

- My leaning: enable the fanout cap flag for the affected tenant segment (CartFwd + any top-10 fanout users) as an emergency protective measure. This is reversible and buys us time to analyze quality impact.

Karthik — can you run a sim offline to estimate the expected model token throughput and quality delta if we cap fanout at 3 for requests with >1 tool call? Also include best- and worst-case p99 improvements in the simulation. We need numbers within the hour so CS can prepare comms.

Grace/Stephanie — start drafting a short, calm message for CartFwd (and siblings) acknowledging investigation + our temporary mitigation. Use this language: "temporary protective caps to reduce latency while we investigate; we expect minimal quality impact but will monitor closely."

I'll authorize the fanout flag for a controlled cohort once we have Karthik's sims. Please update this thread when you have numbers.

—Irene

Irene Choi
Director, Product Operations
irene.choi@redwoodinference.com

> 
> We started seeing a correlated p95/p99 rise on gen-api at ~09:05 PT. Quick summary from the first pass: ...
From: Emily Park <emily.park@cartfwd.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: support@cartfwd.com
Date: Thu, 30 May 2029 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Latency impacting checkout automation (observed 5-10s responses)

Irene —

We're seeing intermittent 5-10s responses in our checkout automation flows that call your /v1/generate endpoint with two tool calls. This started ~09:05 PT and is still happening. It's impacting order throughput and increasing timeouts downstream. Our dev team tried reducing tokens and the issue persisted.

We need: 
- ETA on a mitigation we can rely on for the next 4 hours
- Whether you will throttle or change behavior on our account (please advise if you plan to do so; we need to understand user-impact and rollback plan)

Attaching a short request id list in the drive link (we can share more if you need deeper traces)

—Emily
Emily Park
Sr. Eng Manager, Integrations — CartFwd
emily.park@cartfwd.com

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@cartfwd.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 30 May 2029 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Customer update (draft) — temporary protective caps for fanout-heavy requests

Emily —

Thanks for the heads-up and the example request ids. Short version: we can enable a temporary protective cap on per-request fanout for your tenant cohort while we investigate the root cause. Expected effects: 

- Latency: we expect p99 to improve significantly within 10-20 minutes of the flag (conservative estimate: from ~7s down to ~1.2s for affected flows).
- Quality: multi-tool flows that explicitly rely on cross-tool context may see degraded signal in rare cases. Our simulation suggests <3% classification deviation on your test set for a fanout cap of 3.
- Throughput: small throughput reduction for very large-context requests; most production traffic should be unaffected.

Planned immediate steps (operational timeline):
1) 13:10 PT — enable fanout cap=3 for CartFwd cohort (controlled flag). We will monitor traces and p99 in the next 30 minutes.
2) 13:40 PT — decide whether to expand cap to other affected tenants or rollback.
3) If cap helps, we will run a scoped cache-invalidation rollback candidate in the staging lane for targeted evaluation (requires product signoff).

We are attaching a short diagnostic snapshot and a draft customer note (see attachments). Please let us know if you prefer we hold off on the flag until more analysis is done; otherwise we'll proceed at 13:10 PT and send a short note once the flag is live.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts a critical flow. We'll follow up in this thread with live metrics.

—Irene

Irene Choi
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: cust_brief_draft-20290530.md, diagnostic_snapshot-20290530.log
